paper.title: Transformation to Small-Cell Lung Carcinoma and Then to Sarcomatoid Carcinoma in an EGFR-Mutant Lung Adenocarcinoma Patient During Systemic Therapy: A Case Report.
paper.abstract: This case exemplifies stepwise histological transformations of an initially EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma driven by tumor lineage plasticity under therapeutic pressure. Initial resistance to osimertinib manifested as transformation to combined small-cell lung carcinoma, associated with concurrent TP53/RB1 co-inactivation and the acquisition of an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) C797S mutation. Subsequent progression after chemotherapy featured a rare sarcomatoid transformation, with the tumor retaining the original EGFR Exon 19 deletion, supporting clonal evolution. This phenotypic shift, indicative of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), may have been associated with PTEN loss and potential activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. The serial emergence of neuroendocrine and sarcomatoid phenotypes underscores the critical need for rebiopsy to guide therapy and highlights the profound adaptability of EGFR-mutant tumors, which remain a major therapeutic challenge.

summary.text: This case report describes a patient with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma who developed resistance to osimertinib through transformation to combined small-cell lung carcinoma. This histological shift was driven by tumor lineage plasticity and was associated with concurrent TP53/RB1 co-inactivation and the acquisition of an EGFR C797S mutation.
